quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Driving aggressively.
Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than not driving defensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Maintain your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be alert. Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians crossing the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: Why should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So others can see your vehicle.
To warn others of bad weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: So others can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Headlights make your vehicle easier to see in bad weather. If you use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It lets other drivers know what your intentions are.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets other drivers know what your intentions are.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
Decrease your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks must stop at all railroad crossings. Be ready to stop if you are following one of these vehicles and it stops at railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the part of your brain that controls judgment and skill before it affects other abilities needed for safe driving.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?

options.text: Make abrupt turns.
Apply the brakes firmly.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas, do not brake hard, keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down on its own.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that vehicles in which lane may pass?

options.text: Driving in both directions may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in the fog.
Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware of hazards. Do not stare only at the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: In poor weather conditions, drivers should:

options.text: Increase their speed.
Decrease their speed.
Maintain their normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease their speed.
questions.explanation: You should drive slower in bad weather. Speed limits are set for ideal conditions.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle hydroplanes (rides on water instead of touching the road), slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the right lane is ending. Be ready for merging traffic.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
More slowly than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge at or near the speed of freeway traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction, including bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and maintain your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs warn you of workers and equipment ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following factors affects how quickly someone absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects how they absorb alcohol. Biological sex, the amount of food in the stomach, and how much alcohol someone drinks also matter. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Use only your left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for cars in your blind spot. Look several times before changing lanes. Watch traffic in front of you and in the lane next to you.

questions.question: A solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the center of the road. If the broken line is next to your lane, this means:

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles here.
You can pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns here.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line and broken yellow line mark the center, passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic is merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic will merge from the right.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes. It is good defensive driving.
Yes. It is always safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive so slowly that you block traffic flow, you can be ticketed.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive at the posted speed through the intersection.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
You cannot drive below this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs tell you the maximum speed allowed. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a state road unless posted otherwise?

options.text: 70 mph.
55 mph.
40 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The default speed limit on state roads is 55 mph. Follow posted speed limits if they are different.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
Loose gravel.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
Areas where cars have enough space behind the truck.
Areas where cars have several car lengths from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: What is a driving distraction?

options.text: Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can cause crashes, injuries, and deaths.
